holdem.rules: Everyone gets two private cards; five shared cards come out in three steps (the flop, the turn, the river) with betting between. The best five-card hand wins the pot. Blinds are forced bets that grow every eight hands. All in puts every chip you have in; anything others bet beyond that goes into a side pot you cannot win. Hands from best: royal flush, straight flush, four of a kind, full house, flush, straight, three of a kind, two pair, pair, high card. Chips only, 1000 each to start; last player with chips wins. With two or more people in the Players rows, each sees only their own two cards, behind a handoff.

A new yaku (a scoring combination) lets you call shobu (score now) or koi-koi (play on for more, but the other player may score first). Brights: five 10, four 8 (rainy four 7), three without the rain man 5. Boar-Deer-Butterfly 5, plus 1 per extra animal. Poetry ribbons 5, blue ribbons 5. Moon viewing and flower viewing (the sake cup with the moon or the curtain) 5. Five animals 1, five ribbons 1, ten chaff 1, each extra card 1 more; the sake cup counts as an animal and as chaff. 7 or more doubles; scoring after the other player called koi-koi doubles again. skat.rules: Three players, 32 cards, ten each and two in the skat. Bid by the value of the game you promise (18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 27, 30 ...). The declarer takes the skat, puts two cards back and names a game: a suit (jacks and that suit are trump; clubs 12, spades 11, hearts 10, diamonds 9), grand (only the jacks, 24) or null (no tricks wanted, 23). Playing from the hand without the skat scores more. Ace 11, ten 10, king 4, queen 3, jack 2: the declarer needs 61. Value is the base times the matadors (the top jacks in a row, with or without) plus game, hand, schneider and schwarz. A win scores 50 plus the value; a loss costs 50 plus twice the value and the defenders score 30 each. If all pass, the hand is dealt again. Highest total after the series wins. Tap a card to play it, or drag it to the middle.

tienlen.rules: Four players, 13 cards each. Whoever holds the 3 of spades leads a hand that includes it. Play a single, pair, three or four of a kind, a run of three or more cards in a row, or a run of three or more pairs in a row, matching what is on the table and higher, or pass; a pass keeps you out of that round. Twos are highest (never in a run); suits rank spades, clubs, diamonds, hearts. Chop a two: four of a kind or three pairs in a row beats a single two; four of a kind or four pairs in a row beats a pair of twos. Play goes on until three are out; finishing first to last scores 4, 1, -1, -4. First to 12 wins. Tap cards to pick them, then Play. P plays, S passes, H hints.

tp.rules: Everyone puts in a boot of 10 and gets three cards face down. Play blind (without looking) or look and play seen. The stake starts at 10: a blind player pays the stake (or double to raise it); a seen player pays double, called a chaal (or four times to raise, which doubles the stake). Pack folds. A seen player may ask the seen player before him for a side show: the weaker hand packs (a tie packs the asker). With two players left, Show turns the hands over: the higher wins (a tie goes to the one who did not ask). Hands, best first: trail (three of a kind), pure sequence (straight flush), sequence (straight), colour (flush), pair, high card. A-2-3 is the highest sequence, then A-K-Q down to 4-3-2. {a} plays carefully, {b} boldly and {c} bluffs. If you run short you go all in and the hands are shown. Reach 1500 chips to win, or outlast the others; you lose when you cannot pay the boot.

truco.rules: Three cards each; win two of three tricks. Card order, highest first: ace of swords, ace of clubs, 7 of swords, 7 of coins, then every 3, every 2, the aces of cups and coins, the 12s, 11s and 10s, the other 7s, then the 6s, 5s and 4s. A tied trick goes to whoever wins the next one; later ties go to the first trick’s winner, else to the player who led first (mano). Envido, in the first trick only: two cards of one suit count 20 plus their values, face cards count 0, otherwise your best card counts; the higher total wins (mano on a tie). Envido is worth 2, real envido 3, falta envido what the leader still needs; if the other side declines, you score what was already at stake, at least 1. Truco is worth 2, retruco 3, vale cuatro 4; if the other side declines, you score the value before your call. Fold to give up the hand. Tap a card to play it.
